role.altitude: The nanotechnology technician keeps running experiments, recording deviations, inspecting cleanup sites and adjusting equipment; writing parameters on paper batch records, gauge rounds and filing records shrink.
skills_to_grow: Reading equipment trends and alarms instead of log sheets
Recording deviations clearly in electronic records
role.ambitious_version: A technician whose batch record is complete when the batch ends, so QA can review it the same day.

tasks.short: Record process parameters and materials per batch, record deviations, review the batch record for completeness, have QA approve it and file batch-record documentation of nanoproduction.

steps.what: Nanotechnology technician writes process parameters and material lots on the batch record
Nanotechnology technician records deviations and observations
Nanotechnology technician reviews the batch record for accurate and complete entries
Quality assurance reviewer approves the batch record
Nanotechnology technician files the batch record with test results

tasks.design: An electronic batch record replaces paper. Equipment controllers write setpoints and actual values for each step into the record, and the technician scans material lot barcodes. Fixed checks flag empty fields and values outside specification before the record goes to QA. Deviations are still written by the technician. Test results attach from the test system, and the approved record is stored with its audit trail instead of being scanned and filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Parameters were copied by hand from equipment displays onto paper records.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic batch records linked to equipment controllers and barcode scanners.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a batch behaved differently even when all values were in range.
tasks.altitude: Much less copying; deviation judgement stays.

reach.learn: Whether review time per record falls.

evidence.claim: A test data system records data and produces reports.
Records apps with notifications replace paper logs.

assumptions: Boundary: documenting a batch from run to filing; batch release is QA's decision.

Input contract for s1: setpoints and actual values written by the equipment controllers on about 75% of process steps; manual steps are typed by the technician; lot barcodes on all materials from the warehouse; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s5: test results from the test system linked by batch number.
Deviations keep their full time; QA time is outside the technician's savings.
unknowns: Which equipment can write to the batch record.
research_questions: Do batch records reach QA complete more often?

already_counted.description: Nanotechnology technician resolves flags for missing or out-of-spec values.

incremental.description: Nanotechnology technician keeps batch record templates current with process changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: equipment controllers write values on only half of the process steps, so recording (s1) keeps 63 and the completeness review (s3) keeps 70 (31.7); high: about 75% of steps written by controllers as assumed (43.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collaborate with scientists or engineers to design experiments, prepare samples and equipment, conduct the experiments while recording parameters, and compile results.

steps.what: Nanotechnology technician discusses experiment design with scientists or engineers
Nanotechnology technician prepares samples and equipment
Nanotechnology technician conducts experiments and records parameters
Nanotechnology technician compiles results for the scientists

tasks.design: Instruments write their settings and measurements to the lab's electronic notebook with the run number, so the technician records only what instruments do not. Result tables and plots are generated from the stored runs. Designing experiments with scientists and handling samples stay human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instrument settings and results were copied into notebooks and spreadsheets by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Instruments that export to electronic notebooks and test data systems that generate reports.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what to change in the next run.
tasks.altitude: Little changes at the bench; copying shrinks.

reach.learn: Whether results arrive sooner after runs.

evidence.claim: A test data system records data and produces PDF or Word reports.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing and running experiments; interpretation is the scientists'.
Input contract for s3: instruments that export settings and data to the notebook, about half the instruments; the rest are recorded by hand.
Design talks and sample preparation keep their full time.
research_questions: Do transcription errors in results fall?

incremental.description: Nanotechnology technician maintains instrument export settings.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only a quarter of the instruments export to the notebook, so running and recording (s3) keeps 93 and compiling (s4) keeps 80 (4.9); high: about half of the instruments export as assumed (10.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect the cleanup site and the application of nanocomposites, take samples and readings, record observations and report progress to monitor hazardous waste cleanup procedures against objectives.

steps.what: Nanotechnology technician inspects hazardous waste cleanup procedures and the application of nanocomposites on site
Nanotechnology technician takes samples and field readings
Nanotechnology technician records observations and readings in the field log: on paper today; after the change observations are written in the tablet form and exporting meters import their readings
Nanotechnology technician assesses progress against the cleanup objectives from the log and lab results
Nanotechnology technician writes the progress report for the site engineer in the template, whose tables are filled from the log and results
Nanotechnology technician checks the final progress report: tables match the log and lab results, the assessment says what they show against the objectives, and it goes to the right site engineer
Nanotechnology technician sends the checked progress report to the site engineer

tasks.design: Inspection and sampling stay fully in person. A field form on a tablet records each observation and reading with time, position and photo, and handheld meter readings are imported by cable or Bluetooth instead of written down. Lab results link to the sample numbers, and the progress report template fills tables against objectives from the log and results; the technician writes the assessment.

approvals.approved_version: The progress report with tables and assessment exactly as checked by the technician in s5b, sent once to the site engineer for this cleanup site; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Field notes were written on paper and retyped into reports.
tasks.enabler_now: Field tablets with forms and meter imports.
tasks.still_hard: Judging whether the nanocomposite is working in uneven ground.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting signs on site that the lab will never see.
tasks.altitude: Little changes on site; typing shrinks.

evidence.claim: Reports can fill figures from test and project systems, with each figure traced.

assumptions: Boundary: monitoring cleanup on site and reporting progress; decisions on the remediation are the engineer's.
Input contract for s3: readings from handheld meters that export, about 60% of readings; others are typed into the form. Observations are a first record and keep their full time, so s3 keeps 75.
Input contract for s5: lab results linked by sample number from the contract lab.
Inspection and sampling keep their full time.
s5 keeps 55 because the technician writes the assessment text; checking and sending the report keep their full time.

incremental.description: Nanotechnology technician keeps the field form current with the monitoring plan.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only 30% of meter readings export, so recording (s3) keeps 87, and lab results arrive unlinked, so the report (s5) keeps 75 (3.1); high: about 60% of readings exported and linked results as assumed (6.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Walk the equipment and read gauges, log pressure, temperature and flow values, adjust settings when values drift and report deviations to monitor equipment during operation against specifications.

steps.what: Nanotechnology technician monitors equipment by walking it and reading pressure, temperature and flow gauges
Nanotechnology technician writes the readings on the log sheet; after the change only local gauges are written, and sensor values are logged by the historian
Nanotechnology technician adjusts settings when values drift from specifications
Nanotechnology technician writes the deviation report for the engineer, with the historian trend linked instead of copied values
Nanotechnology technician checks the final deviation report: the values, times and settings changed match the log and historian, and it goes to the responsible engineer
Nanotechnology technician sends the checked deviation report to the engineer

tasks.design: Sensors on the equipment feed the control system's historian, which logs pressure, temperature and flow continuously and raises alarms outside specification limits, so rounds focus on local gauges and checks the sensors do not cover. Log sheets go for parameters on sensors. Adjusting settings and reporting deviations stay with the technician. Alarms are fixed limits, not a model.

approvals.approved_version: The deviation report with values, times and settings changed exactly as checked by the technician in s4b, sent once to the responsible engineer; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Values were read on rounds and written on log sheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Process historians with limit alarms on the control system.
tasks.still_hard: Drift that stays within limits but signals trouble.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing or smelling that equipment is not right.
tasks.altitude: Fewer rounds and log sheets; responding to drift stays.

reach.learn: Whether continuous trends reveal causes of drift.

evidence.claim: AI-powered safety functions in machinery fall under the Machinery Regulation from 20 January 2027; fixed alarms are not AI.
Process historians log sensor values and raise limit alarms.

assumptions: Boundary: monitoring and adjusting running equipment; maintenance is outside.
Input contract for s1 and s2: sensors connected to the control system on about 75% of monitored parameters; local gauges are still read and logged on rounds; s1 and s2 are priced at that share.

Adjusting keeps its full time; writing the deviation report keeps 90 because the trend is linked instead of copied; checking and sending it keep their full time. s2 keeps 30: writing local gauges plus glancing at the historian log on each round.

incremental.description: Nanotechnology technician reviews alarm limits with the engineer.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: sensors cover only half of the monitored parameters, so rounds (s1) keep 73 and log sheets (s2) keep 53 (20.1); high: about 75% covered as assumed (29.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
